extracted.intended_audience: public-company registrants, preparers of SEC filings, and their legal/accounting advisors evaluating/reporting acquisitions under SEC rules (Form 8-K, registration statements)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and interpretive criteria for determining whether an acquisition constitutes a 'business' for SEC reporting purposes and for identifying related filing requirements (S-X Rule 3-05, S-X Rule 11-01, Rule 3-14). Includes examples and factors applied to asset purchases, leases, investments, VIEs, real estate, oil & gas, insurance blocks, bankrupt entities, joint ventures, and step acquisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of operations (SEC definition of a business)
rubrics_metrics.description: Focuses on whether there is sufficient continuity of operations before and after the transaction. A key principle is whether disclosure of prior financial information is material to an understanding of future operations. [S-X Rule 11-01(d)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied across examples: if the acquirer intends to continue the seller's operations (printing facility, distribution, customer service, revenue-producing activities), the acquisition is more likely a business; if assets are acquired for inputs into the acquirer's existing operations (e.g., early-stage molecules, cost-center data processing) and the acquirer does not intend to continue the seller's business, the acquisition may not be a business for SEC reporting purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: US GAAP definition vs SEC reporting definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The definitions of a business under SEC Regulations and under US GAAP are distinct: SEC focuses on continuity of operations and materiality of prior financial information; US GAAP (Topic 805) uses a two-step test (Step 1 concentrate-in-single-asset test; Step 2 whether an integrated set of activities and assets is capable of being conducted and managed to provide a return and includes inputs and processes applied to those inputs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An acquired set may be a business under US GAAP but not be a business for SEC reporting purposes (or vice versa). Registrants must evaluate under the applicable definition for SEC filing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predecessor designation (when required and factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation of a predecessor is required if a registrant succeeds to substantially all of the business of another entity and the registrant's own operations before succession appear insignificant relative to the operations assumed or acquired. [FRM 1170.1]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple acquisitions occur, determine which target entity is the predecessor. SEC staff expects robust disclosures about the predecessor determination. Key factors include relative size and fair value of targets, historical and ongoing management structure, and order in which entities were acquired. No single factor is determinative; multiple businesses may be co‑predecessors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single asset (or group of assets) can constitute a business
rubrics_metrics.description: In some circumstances, the acquisition of an asset (or group of assets) that generates a revenue-producing activity may constitute the acquisition of a business (e.g., acquisition of oil and gas interests or property leasehold interests with in-place operations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the asset(s) generate revenue-producing activity and whether there is continuity of that activity after acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset acquisition vs business acquisition for S-X Rule 3-05
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquisition of an asset (or group of assets) that does not meet the SEC definition of a business is not subject to the requirements of S-X Rule 3-05. However, a registrant must report a significant (10% level) asset acquisition under Item 2.01 of Form 8-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if not a 'business' for Rule 3-05, registrants must consider other reporting rules (Form 8-K Item 2.01) and legal determinations about materiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil and gas interests — generally businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC staff generally considers the acquisition of a working interest in a producing oil and gas property to be a business for SEC reporting purposes. Acquisition of undeveloped acreage with no associated production may not be a business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a transaction includes both producing property and undeveloped acreage, the staff has not objected to separating the transaction into two acquisitions (producing properties vs undeveloped acreage) only if the acquisition is not of an entire entity or substantially all assets; consult legal counsel and consider pre-clearance with the SEC staff if applying separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bank branch acquisition — fact-dependent
rubrics_metrics.description: The acquisition of part or all of a bank branch may be the acquisition of a business if the acquired activities are the primary source of revenue for the branch or the bank. An assumption of customer deposits may also be the acquisition of a business if historical revenue-producing activity is reasonably traceable to the management or customer/deposit base and will remain generally the same following the acquisition. [FRM 2010.5]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If branch revenues derive from activities not acquired, acquiring deposits alone may not constitute a business acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block of insurance policies — may be a business
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquisition of a block of insurance policies by an insurer, or assumption of policy liabilities in reinsurance, may be the acquisition of a business because the right to receive future premiums generally indicates continuity of historical revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the degree of continuity between historical investment income streams and the assets acquired to fund the acquired policy liabilities. [FRM 2010.6]

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition of a bankrupt entity — depends on facts
rubrics_metrics.description: No specific guidance; evaluate using the same principle as other acquisitions — whether the revenue-producing activity will be substantially the same after the acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bankrupt entity is likely a business if it had revenue-producing activities during bankruptcy and will continue the same activities after acquisition. If it did not have revenue-producing activities during bankruptcy, assess whether prior financial information about the entity is material to understanding its future operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition by lease of operating assets — business if risks/rewards transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquisition of operations through execution of a lease of operating assets (instead of purchase) is the acquisition of a business for SEC reporting purposes if the lease transfers to the lessee substantially all the risks and rewards of the ongoing operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases there generally will be continuity of revenue-producing processes or activities after the acquisition, making prior financial information material. Registrant-lessee may need to consolidate the lessor if the lessor is a VIE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business acquired in the form of a lease — example factors
rubrics_metrics.description: If a lessee (e.g., nursing home manager) leases real estate, assumes all risks/rewards and responsibilities for working capital, and guarantees facility debt, the registrant concludes it is acquiring a business for SEC reporting purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even without ownership of real estate, acquiring substantially all risks and rewards of operations indicates acquisition of a business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of a VIE — may be acquisition of a business
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition of a controlling financial interest in a VIE (or initial consolidation of a VIE due to reconsideration under Subtopic 810-10) is the acquisition of a business if there is sufficient continuity of operations such that prior financial information about the entity is material to understanding its future operations. This is the case even if the registrant paid or issued no consideration. [FRM 2005.8]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a newly consolidated VIE is not a business for SEC reporting purposes, a registrant may still need to report the consolidation on Form 8-K if material to investors' understanding of future operations. Consolidation on adoption of a new/amended accounting standard affecting Subtopic 810-10 does not trigger Form 8-K filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial investment in debt or equity securities — not a business
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquisition of a debt or equity security accounted for under Topic 320 (debt securities) or Topic 321 (equity securities) is not the acquisition of a business for SEC reporting purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider other reporting obligations if the acquisition is material to investor understanding of future operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition of an equity method investment — depends on underlying investee
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial purchase of an investment accounted for under the equity method is considered the acquisition of a business for SEC reporting purposes if the underlying investee is a business per the SEC's definition. This also applies when the registrant elects the fair value option in lieu of the equity method. [S-X Rule 3-05(a)(2)(ii)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the investee is not a business, the acquisition may still be reportable on Form 8-K if material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step acquisitions / increases in existing equity investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Increases in existing equity investments can be the acquisition of a business if the underlying investee is a business. Outcomes include: (a) financial instrument before and equity method or consolidation after — acquisition of a business; (b) equity method before and equity method or consolidation after — acquisition of a business; (c) consolidated subsidiary before and after — an increase is also acquisition of a business for significance testing and potential reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an increase results in initial application of the equity method or consolidation, the purchase transaction represents acquisition of a business. Even if consolidated financial statements already include the acquired business, pro forma financial statements may be required. Registrants performing significance tests should consider implications for Rule 3-05 and pro forma requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition of joint venture interest — treated as business acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquiring an interest in a joint venture is considered the acquisition of a business for SEC reporting purposes. Formation of a joint venture is deemed two transactions: (1) disposition of assets/business contributed to the joint venture (to the extent of the other partner's economic interest) and (2) acquisition of an equity method investment in a business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disposition component may require Form 8-K if significant. See section 3.7.30 for significance calculation considerations related to joint venture interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating real estate — excluded from S-X Rule 3-05; use Rule 3-14
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-05 specifically excludes acquisitions of operating real estate, which are subject to the requirements of S-X Rule 3-14 (Special Instructions for financial statements of real estate operations acquired or to be acquired).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 3-14 reduced financial statement requirements are premised on continuity and predictability of cash flows ordinarily associated with commercial and apartment property leasing. Other types of real estate investments (nursing homes, hotels, motels, golf courses, auto dealerships, equipment rental operations) are generally not considered real estate operations for Rule 3-14 due to greater revenue/cost variability and may be subject to Rule 3-05 instead. See examples distinguishing scenarios where acquisition of hotels was a business vs where leasing property to an operator resulted in real estate operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity interest in preexisting entity holding real estate — depends on activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition of an interest in a preexisting legal entity that holds only real estate under lease and related debt generally represents acquisition of real estate operations subject to Rule 3-14. If the entity engages in other activities (property management, development), evaluate whether it meets the SEC's definition of a business (continuity of operations). [FRM 2305.3]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If determined to be a business and acquisition is significant, Rule 3-05 financial statements are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment in newly formed entity that plans to acquire real estate — generally not a business (Rule 3-14 applies)
rubrics_metrics.description: An investment in a newly formed partnership or corporation that will acquire real estate properties under lease simultaneously with or soon after formation is generally viewed as the acquisition of real estate operations; SEC staff requires Rule 3-14 financial statements of the underlying property rather than Rule 3-05 financial statements of the newly formed entity. This assumes the new entity has no other activities besides leasing real property. [FRM 2305.4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of other activities could result in a different determination; evaluate facts and circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-05(a) — financial statement filing triggers and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements (audited, prepared under Regulation S-X) of businesses acquired or to be acquired must be filed for the periods specified if: (i) during the most recent fiscal year or subsequent interim period a business acquisition has occurred; or (ii) after the date of the most recent balance sheet, consummation of a business acquisition has occurred or is probable. Determination of whether a business has been acquired should be made per §210.11-01(d). Acquisition of an interest in a business accounted for under the equity method (or fair value option) is encompassed. Acquisitions of related businesses subsequent to fiscal year-end must be treated as a single business acquisition if related (common control/management, conditional acquisitions, or conditioned on a common event).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule excludes real estate operations subject to §210.3-14 or a business totally held by the registrant prior to consummation.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 11-01 — pro forma financial information filing triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma financial information must be filed when any of the enumerated conditions exist, including: (1) during the most recent fiscal year or subsequent interim period a significant business acquisition has occurred; (2) after the date of the most recent balance sheet consummation of a significant business acquisition or combination under common control has occurred or is probable; (3) securities being registered are to be offered to holders of a significant business to be acquired; (4) disposition of a significant portion of a business has occurred or is probable and not fully reflected in registrant financials; (6) pro forma required for roll-up transactions; (7) registrant previously was part of another entity and presentation needed to reflect autonomous operations; (8) consummation of other transactions where pro forma would be material to investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-X Rule 3-05(a) and S-X Rule 11-01(a) can both be triggered by business acquisitions: 3-05 requires filing of financial statements of the acquired business when significant; 11-01 requires pro forma information reflecting the combination when significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance testing and required steps after determining a business acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a registrant determines it has acquired a business, it must perform the significance tests (described in chapter 3) to determine reporting requirements for the acquisition (e.g., whether Rule 3-05 financial statements are required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document references a >20% significance threshold in example tables; registrants should follow the significance calculation guidance in chapter 3 and related sections (e.g., 3.7.30 for joint ventures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider when evaluating whether revenue-producing activity remains generally the same
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the nature of the revenue-producing activity will remain generally the same after the transaction, along with other facts and circumstances (e.g., what assets transfer, whether shore-based facilities remain, whether acquirer is already in the same business, number of employees hired, number and terms of customer contracts, other attributes transferred, and whether historical operating performance is meaningful for future performance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (ships): differences in business model (hourly vs long-term charters), limited transfer of shore facilities and employees, short remaining contract terms, and expected changes in people/processes supported the conclusion that the acquisition of ships was not a business for SEC reporting purposes.
